interpretation: Repeated-seed confirmation: means, sample standard deviations and ranges describe the recorded seeds. Each comparison uses within-seed ratios; no confidence intervals or population claims are inferred from these repeats.
limitations: Short fixed-global-batch timing runs do not establish convergence, quality equivalence, or research novelty.
Single-host measurements do not establish multi-node network scaling.
TP uses all ranks on one microbatch; DDP/FSDP/sharded AdamW partition the global batch. All use the recorded global batch.
Sharded AdamW shards optimizer state only; its full parameters and gradients remain replicated.

TP and FSDP initialize a full FP32 model on every GPU before sharding. Training memory savings do not demonstrate initialization of models larger than one GPU can hold; reserved memory can retain the setup allocator cache.
timing_note: Each optimizer step follows an inter-rank barrier and device synchronization. Reported time is the maximum rank time, including data, backward synchronization, clipping, update and loss reduction; it excludes the timing-max reduction, evaluation, setup and checkpoint writes. This measures synchronized steps, not uninterrupted end-to-end training throughput.
cost_note: Active GPU-seconds per update = participating GPUs × measured training seconds / measured updates. All allocated GPUs are billed even during a one-GPU baseline. Allocated GPU-seconds for subprocesses include process startup and evaluation, but not all launch overhead. Function-time dollar estimates use the launch's recorded requested-resource rate; they are not invoices and exclude image builds, startup, excess CPU/RAM, storage/egress and other apps.
